question: Estimate the bandwidth a 5G telco needs to provision in Mumbai per square km.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Frame the approach
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Users per sq km × peak per-user usage.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Mumbai average density: ~22M people / 600 sq km = ~37,000 people per sq km.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Per-user peak hour throughput (5G era, video heavy): ~3-5 Mbps sustained.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Considering oversubscription (not all users 100% concurrent): ~50% effective = ~50 Gbps per sq km.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Telco share (3 telcos in market): each provisions ~15-20 Gbps per sq km.

benchmarkAssumptions.value: ~22M people / 600 sq km = ~37,000 people per sq km.

benchmarkAssumptions.parameter: Of these, smartphone-internet active during peak hour
Per-user peak hour throughput (5G era, video heavy)

benchmarkAssumptions.value: each provisions ~15-20 Gbps per sq km.

calculationFlow: Mumbai average density: ~22M people / 600 sq km = ~37,000 people per sq km.
Of these, smartphone-internet active during peak hour: ~70% = ~26K users/sq km.
Per sq km peak demand: 26K × 4 Mbps = ~100 Gbps per sq km.
Considering oversubscription (not all users 100% concurrent): ~50% effective = ~50 Gbps per sq km.

finalAnswerRange.ideal: Telco share (3 telcos in market): each provisions ~15-20 Gbps per sq km.
